article: Luke sat at his computer. The keys were slicked from the oil of one too many cheetos, his right hand moving the mouse sporadically along its pad while his left tapped the same four keys over and over. His eyes were focused on the game, leaving only momentarily to move toward his bag of chips or reach for his mountain dew. He would bring it to his lips with his eyes focused on the screen until there was a knock at the door and even then they just glanced up before returning their focus to his game. When it was over Luke brought the back of his hand up to his forehead and wiped away the sweat from his adrenaline. There was a knock on his door. His mother opened it without asking, as she always did. "Luke, come on. It's time to go to school." "Not going. I'm sick today," Luke gave a halfhearted cough. His mother sighed, moving inside his room with her arms crossed and standing against his wall so that he could just see her out of his peripheral vision. "Luke, this isn't a conversation. You're going to school. Change out of those sweatpants and wash your face and go to school." "I'm sick." "Then we're seeing the doctor." Luke groaned, pressing his head back. His temple was already bulging. He hadn't slept the night before, planning to stay up all night and tire his mother out by claiming he was sick. "Fine, I'll go see the stupid doctor." "And you're not using your computer all day." "What?" "You heard me. No computer. If you're sick you can stay in bed and read and catch up on some of the homework that you've missed." "Mom, that's not fair." Luke felt his face begin to heat up. This had not been part of the plan. "And you'll stay in the downstairs bedroom while you do it. No computer in there. No phone games. Just your homework or a book. Or you can watch a DVD and mdash;" "I need my computer to do homework," Luke whined. "No you don't," his mother said. "Now go wash your face and change and I'm taking you to school." Luke made his way down the hallway, adjusting himself as he went. By the time he reached the bathroom his breath was labored and heavy. He stood looking at himself in the mirror - at his pimply face and his greasy hair and his perpetually neon-orange fingertips. He could see the outline of his hand on his groin, the sweat that built along his neckline and stained his shirt, the yellow that gathered under his armpits. His nostrils flared as he looked down, turning on the sink and washing his face. It's not like it will help with the stupid acne, he thought. Nothing he did seemed to help with that. Fucking ugly piece of dirt. Luke hated school. The desks weren't big enough for his gut, and he was always acutely aware of how it spilled over onto the desk. He wore his hat low over his eyes to hide his greasy hair until his teachers told him to take it off. He would, feeling his cheeks boiling as what felt like every pair of eyes turned to him. There was a girl at school named Monica who Luke had a crush on. They had biology together, and she was one of the only people who had ever been nice to him. She was one of those popular girls, with perfect makeup and up to date fashion sense. When he faked sick so many days she would keep his homework assignments together and give them to him. He was in love with her. He opened doors for her and called her m'lady to make her feel special. He treated her like the Queen he was because Luke knew that Monica saw him for who he really was. Sometimes he would bring her small gifts - little flowers that he had picked from trees or origami swans that he had made. She always seemed to appreciate them. That day at school she came up to him after biology. "Hey, Luke. I picked up your homework assignments from the last few days. You okay? You've been out a lot." "Yeah, I'm fine," Luke said. He tipped his fedora to Monica in a way of thanks. She smiled and turned away. "Hey, Monica," Luke swallowed. She's not going to say yes. What are you doing? What are you doing? "I..... I know we don't talk much. But. Well. I was wondering if you wanted to go out sometime. If you want to get coffee or something. I'm a really nice guy, you'll see if you get to know me. I'll buy you stuff and mdash;" "Oh Luke, I'm sorry. I have a boyfriend. I thought you knew, I just mdash;" "Know, I know. I know. But he doesn't treat you well. He couldn't treat you as well as I'd treat you, Monica. You know that. He doesn't give you the attention you deserve." Monica looked down to the floor. "I've been with Sam for three years, Luke. I'm sorry, but the answer is no." Luke felt his face flush. "Why not? You're always flirting with me, giving me my homework and taking those little presents I give you. You act totally in to me but I guess you don't want to be seen with me, huh? You're embarrassed by me. But the truth is I'd treat you better than Sam ever will. I'd be the best thing that happened to you in your life." Monica's smile had vanished. "The best thing that happened to me in my life was my little brother beating cancer." Her voice was cold. "You think you deserve me because I bring you homework and you're a nice guy? You just tried to convince me to leave my boyfriend of three years. Screw you." Luke put his head down on the desk after she left, feeling a single tear fall down his cheek. Why don't I ever get anything that I want? he thought. Somewhere in France the world's tiniest violin was playing. - [ Surprise ] (s "There was no surprise.

article: Importance of visual context in scene understanding tasks is well recognized in the computer vision community. However, to what extent the computer vision models for image classification and semantic segmentation can accurately understand the visual context depends on various factors, including the complexity of the scene, the diversity of objects and their interactions, and the quality of the training data. In simpler scenes, where the objects and their relationships are clearly defined, a computer vision model can accurately predict the object classes and their locations. However, in complex scenes where multiple objects are present and their relationships are intricate, the accuracy of the models decreases. This is because the models require not only visual cues but also contextual cues such as spatial relationships and semantic relationships to determine the correct object class and its spatial location. Hence, the importance of visual context increases in such cases. Furthermore, the quality of the training data is crucial as the computer vision models rely on labeled data to learn the object classes, their semantic relationships, and their spatial locations. Inaccurate or insufficient training data can lead to poor performance of the models. In conclusion, while the recognition of the importance of visual context in scene understanding tasks is well-established, the accuracy of the computer vision models for image classification and semantic segmentation depends on various factors, including scene complexity, diversity of objects, quality of training data, and the ability of models to incorporate contextual cues.
label: machine

article: Edit: I apologise for any spelling mistakes. I wrote this when I was very tired. "If you could take a seat Mr Simmons, we'll have you through to the memory recollection suite in a few minutes" I smiled at the bubbly receptionist before calming stating "Thank you." I had expected them to be ready for me there and then, so I awkwardly made my way to the seating area. I was trying to force my body language to be relaxed and comfortable, not scream out the worry and anxiety rolling through my head, but I doubt I was succeeding. Discovering I had memory missing had been the strangest thing, like waking from a dream almost. Four years had gone without me ever realising. At least I think its been four years, because that's when my memory gets blurry. So I assume it's that long..... In a dream there are things wrong that you just accept - because you're dreaming and it makes sense when you're in that world - yet that had been my reality. No recollection of my birthplace, highschool, just lots of half memories about places I had been and bizarre stories that only seemed impossible when someone else questioned them. Explaining it to people left a skeptical look on their face, had them judging my intellect and it had taken almost an hour to have my local doctor actually scan my brain to discover I was telling the truth. As soon as the scan results came onto the screen however the look on his face dropped, and he immediately called the nearest central hospital, telling me to leave the clinic that instant. Trying to retain his calm the Doctor had blurted out "It appears almost your entire brain has been tampered with" He shook his head at his own statement "It's impossible to tell how much of what you know is real or not. You need to get to the hospital right away, and I'm sorry but I'm going to have to call the police as well." I had just nodded and agreed as I was rushed out the clinic. Having driven numbly to the Hospital, here I was, now wondering what terrible crime I had committed that I would wipe my mind. What sort of evil person was I? Had I been part of a conspiracy? Wh- "Mr Simmons?" "Hmm? Oh yes, umm, coming. Right away" I pushed myself up and rubbed my hands together. I bit my lip softly as I headed through the doors with the nurse who had called my name and found myself searching for something to talk about. Just to ease my nerves. "Umm. The police they "They're on their way yes, sorry about that sir but in a case this serious we have to assume the worst. Memory deletion is an incredibly complicated and expensive process, costing tens of millions for even the most basic of operations but you..." She glanced over at me and I realised she was speaking so rapidly and openly because she was scared of me "You've had such intense surgery we aren't even sure where you could have gone to get it done, I mean, the recovery process is a simple electrical stimulation, I mean, well electrical stim- well." She blinked as she tried to form proper sentences, but failed as we came to a door. She opened it and waited. She didn't appear to be joining me. It was then I noticed a black shape at the edge of her uniform. She had a gun. That wasn't normal for nurses, just what could I have locked away in this head of mine? Who was I? What had other people been that forced these actions? "Good luck" She smiled meekly. I swallowed hard enough for it to be a sound as I entered a room, walking towards the table that- ..... I blinked, recoiling from the bright light as I came to. There was a doctor to my side smiling who asked "There. You should have your memory flooding back any second now. I told you it wouldn't be any problem" Dazed I sat up slowly. "What? When did you say that?" "Oh you're having a'reverse switch', you forget the start of the procedure and then it should..." His voice faded into the dark as suddenly I felt my mind start to expand. It wasn't like someone opening up flood gates, it was like a mighty dam exploding and destroying everything in its path. Memories from all ages came thundering through all at once making me gasp and choke, grabbing the side of the table as I tried to find balance. The doctor was trying to shout at me about something but the noise inside my head drowned him out as the surge of memories tensed my whole body. As I remembered who I was, who I truly was. I realised just how terrified the doctors must have been, and as more memories returned I started to notice body language movements, subtler hints. My day job started to seem unimportant, the doctor slow, and this procedure inefficient. It was several minutes before I breathed out peacefully. My mind now whole. I opened my eyes. The police were on their way. I needed to get out of here right now. If they managed to get their hands on a Time Traveller like myself, who knew what incredible damage could be caused.

article: The park ranger told us as we crossed the river, the water reaching just below our knees, that we were almost at the campsite. This was good, because I was feeling like I was going to collapse under the weight of my rucksack. At the other side of the river we made ourselves carefully through rocks once submerged in the water, shoes squelching, shivering from the cold wind. We soon came out onto a clearing surrounded tightly by pine trees. I took off my shoes and let the grass scratch my itchy souls. I thought I was going to get a fungal infection but the ranger took one look at my feet and said I was fine. I tiptoed to the fire Sandy made and went as close possible to the flames. The sun was below the horizon by the time the boys came back with an antelope on their shoulders. The ranger nodded encouragingly as Sandy and I prepared a meat and mushroom stew and as the boys set up the tents. He told me the mushrooms helped with infections in case one of us acquired one. He had his hand on my shoulder, was stiflingly close. For a moment it seemed like he was succeeding in pulling me in, but then I blinked and walked away. He was really starting to make me feel uncomfortable. One of the boys was my boyfriend, I didn't need this. I insisted to be on watch duty because I wanted to cool after hours of sitting next to the fire. There were no clouds to block out the stars. It seemed like the stars were moving, in circular motions. I started to giggle and I wanted to call Sandy to come take a look but the words melted into each other and sounded sluggish. I shrugged and looked up. The stars were now growing and shrinking and the moon shrunk and exploded to smithereens. He came out of his tent, wearing only a short. He took my wrist and helped me up, guided me to his tent. I was excited; maybe there'd be a magical lion with wings waiting in there or whatever. He made me lie on my back and the excitement was almost unbearable but I couldn't see a lion, I saw only large eyes watching me, thousands of them. He took off my jeans, his hands were rougher than my boyfriend's. I felt something pull me and then I sat up but he hushed me back onto the ground. My body tensed and then I pushed his head away from my face and screamed the names of the others. But was that my voice? Or someone else's? Were those even words I said? He was fighting with me, put a hand over my mouth. I struggled and struggled and that's when I heard something outside. It was the magical lion, I could hear the growls, saw its prowling shadow against the canvas. The ranger froze.The tent was torn apart and the magical lion jumped on the ranger and hugged him. But the ranger was screaming. Who screams when given a hug? Maybe he didn't want it. Yes, he didn't want it, let him scream. I'm pulled up weakly by Sandy, I can see her groggy face, she looks high. Me too, maybe? She's saying something with effort: we have to run. I wave to the ranger and the lion. The lion waves back, a flamboyant wiggling of its paw, but the ranger doesn't.

article: The day before I took the test my family threw a huge party. We lived in a nice neighborhood in the 130 district, and life had been pretty good. article: Gage sat up suddenly. Scary movies, haunted houses, frightening novels, - he found enticing. He chose them. Forcing himself to be afraid, to face his fears, was something he enjoyed. Nightmares were a different thing completely. With a nightmare, he had no choice. He found the lack of control, as a horror unfolded within the synapses of his mind, left him feeling weak and powerless. He pursued fear because he wanted to have power over it. He did not want it to have power over him. In his nightmares, his choices gone, it did. "Stop being a baby!" He said to himself. It wasn't that this nightmare had been particularly scary. In the dream, there was only a brown a paper bag siting alone in he middle of the floor. His dream self, had reached into the bag only to have his hand grabbed by another. A hand that was green and lizard like - almost alien in structure and form. It was stupid really. He laughed at himself, as he sat in his bed, his white t-shirt sticky and see through with sweat. Still laughing, he got up to pee. Opening the bedroom door he moved towards the hall - what he saw on the hall floor made his stop. "Eeeeeeeeh." He screamed, as he sucked in air, almost squealing. He was surprised that such a feminine sound came from his mouth. He stared at the brown paper bag, partly crumpled with the top folded slightly. It was the size of a grocery bag, but had no label. It looked eerily like the bag from his dream. He continued to stare at the bag. "You're being a baby." He said to himself. "Just open the bag." He didn't move. "Come on man. This ain't a dream. You are in control....and you got ta pee. Now just look in the bag." He still didn't move. "Okay it is time to man up. Now come on. You'd make fun of somebody acting like this. It's just a bag." He looked inside his doorway and found a metal hanger on the floor. Grabbing it tightly he turned back toward the bag. Bending over just a bit, he poked the bag with the metal hanger. And then...... ....... Nothing happened. He started laughing to himself and poked the bag again. Still nothing. He put the hanger down. Gage bent further over and grasped the bag. He carefully unfolded and pulled it open as it's brown fibers made a crunching sound. He spread the mouth of the bag wide. Inside he found the source of his fear, two dusty wingtip shoes, courtesy of his messy roommate. He laughed harder, bent over in the hall, looking at the shoes. In one motion, a strong green hand grasped his ankle as another covered his mouth and pulled him backwards, still hunched over, and launched him into his room. He never had time to scream. He was never in control.

article: There was always going to come a time that I'd simply had enough. The worst part wasn't the bullying. That, I could handle. I had 3 older brothers, so I was used to it being a bit rough. It's the blatant ignoring that I couldn't stand. When I asked to sit at a table at lunch, I got completely blanked. When it was time to pair up for a project, I was always the last man left. And just forget prom, or anything along those lines. Girls treated me with the same ignorance as the guys. I once heard someone say the opposite of love isn't hate; it's indifference. Sounds legit to me. So I decided I would do something to make them notice me. I've got the gun tucked away in my school bag. Between a science textbook and my lunch. I feel like that's kind of funny, and I smile. My mother notices. She's been worried about me, and I bet she thinks I've met a girl I like. On the bus, I'm pretty nervous. I wonder if this is normal? I can't exactly ask anyone. Maybe, if I change my mind at the last minute and decide not to take my own life, there'll be support groups I can join. I've decided that the best time to do this is during the afternoon assembly, when all the students gather in the auditorium to hear announcements and whatever. Most bang for my buck that way. But it does mean I need to keep the gun concealed until then. This amuses me more, like I have a special secret. I spend my lunch in the library. The lady who works there, Donna, has never been outright mean to me, but I think she thinks I'm weird. I'm pretty sure she isn't allowed to actually say anything though. So this is where I always eat lunch. No one to judge me here. It's getting closer to the end of the school year, which means exams are coming up, so there's more people here studying than normal. There's Jack in the corner. I'm not really convinced he knows how to read, but his beautiful girlfriend, Jenny, is sitting with him. I guess she's reading to him. At another desk, there's Anna, shy and quiet with huge glasses. She reminds me of an owl. I didn't think she'd ever need to study. Must be about 18 people in here today. About 15 more than normal. I scan them all, and again I'm amused. They don't know what's coming. What would they do if they did know? I stand up to get ready to go to my next class. Just one more to go before the deed. At exactly the same time, I see Adrian Denny stand up from his desk. Another loner, Adrian does more to separate himself than anyone I know. He's gone for a bit of a goth look, and he's the only kid I know in our school with a tattoo. We lock eyes for a moment. He starts to slowly reach into his bag, and it's like everything is in slow motion. Somehow, I know what's coming. I see a glint of metal as he pulls his hand out, and I yell ' GET DOWN!!' Some are quicker to react than others. Anna quickly dives under a desk, and I see Jack trying to pull Jenny behind the librarian's desk. She isn't fast enough, and the first shot rings out, making its way right into Jenny's perfectly tanned leg. The screams start then, and I can see there's a divide between people who are trying to exit the library, and those just trying to hide. The people trying to get away get the next tirade of bullets. Becky and Mason go down straight away, their wails adding to the cacophony. Alex gets grazed by a bullet, but carries on, getting out of the room and sounding the alarm in the hallways. ' DENNY'S GOT A GUN!' More screams. Everything still seems to be in slow motion for me. Adrian's gone after one of the students, almost chasing him around the racks of books. article: Imitation learning has traditionally been applied to learn a single task from demonstrations thereof. The requirement of structured and isolated demonstrations limits the scalability of imitation learning approaches as they may not generalize well to new or complex situations. However, recent developments in imitation learning such as behavior cloning and inverse reinforcement learning have enabled broader and more diverse use cases. Behavior cloning involves simply copying the actions from demonstration data to learn a policy. This approach can be effective for simple tasks with clear demonstrations, but it can also result in a lack of flexibility in handling novel situations. In contrast, inverse reinforcement learning involves trying to deduce the underlying reward function of the demonstrator given their behavior. This approach can lead to more generalizable policies that can handle novel situations. Furthermore, developments in multi-task and meta learning have allowed imitation learning to be applied more effectively to tasks with complex and diverse sets of skills. These approaches allow the agent to learn to learn, or to learn to transfer skills learned from one task to another. Overall, imitation learning continues to evolve as a promising approach for developing intelligent systems and has the potential to revolutionize industries such as robotics, autonomous driving, and more.

article: Abundant data is the key to successful machine learning. However, supervised learning requires annotated data that are often hard to obtain. Active Learning is an iterative process that involves selecting a subset of unlabeled samples to be labeled by an expert or crowd-sourced annotators, and then incorporating this newly annotated data back into the model to improve its accuracy. The goal is to improve the model's performance while minimizing the number of labeled samples needed. One common Active Learning algorithm is uncertainty sampling, where the model selects the samples with the highest uncertainty as the most informative examples to be labeled. This is based on the assumption that the model is uncertain about the correct label for these samples, therefore labeling them will provide the most valuable information to improve the model's accuracy. Other Active Learning strategies may also consider diversity or representative sampling, selecting samples that are dissimilar or representative of the data distribution to ensure the model learns a diverse range of examples. Overall, active learning is a powerful approach to optimize resource allocation and accelerate the process of building accurate machine learning models with limited resources.

article: Dear mom, I took a girl out for our first date tonight. I think it went well. She's really wonderful. She's poised, intelligent, has a great sense of humor (as in she thinks my goofiness is charming..... so potentially delusional). She's beautiful, but not just in the normal sense. Her smile lights up a room and best of all God shines through her and I see an authentic love for people and her personal faith. You came up. I didn't want to tell her too much. It has happened more than once that I tell a woman about my relationship with you and they run. I don't blame them, but I really didn't want this girl to run. For the longest time I wondered if I'd ever be able to have a healthy romantic relationship, if I'd ever find a wife, if I'd ever get over my distrust of women because of you. Every time I avoided getting too close to a girl out of fear, every time I was a nervous wreck half wishing the girl wouldn't show for a meet up, all the times I heard the lies you planted in me that I wasn't worth a woman's love (partially out of guilt for how you made me feel I was treating you); I cursed you. I'm past the part of my life where I'm angry and want to "get back at you." I'm writing you this because I was overjoyed at this evening spent with Martha and..... and I'm brought to tears that I can't excitedly tell you about it the next morning. A grown man that should be past such sentimental silly things feels strongly the wound you made with a childhood of abuse. Mom, I know I've been cold-hearted, that is true. God urges me to be compassionate and I have wanted to have my revenge so badly. But this is my triumph. Mom, I know you are a fallen person. Even if you will not acknowledge the pain you've put me through, I forgive you. I choose to forgive the hurtful words you spoke about me. I actively process the pain you've put me through in order to truly release it. I choose to forgive the violence you used to intimidate me as well as all the times you used flawed interpretations of scripture to manipulate me. I choose to release the burden I've put upon myself when I neglected to forgive you all these years. Anything else I'm forgetting to specifically mention or that is just adding to the list to where it begins to just be me complaining, it's gone, forget about it. I just want my mommy, like when I was eight and needed you to kiss my boo boos. Or like when I needed advice on girls becoming a teenager, or when I needed you to help me so many other times in so many ways but I couldn't come to you. I want to be happy about the possibility of you coming to my wedding and I don't want to cringe thinking of you being around my children. To sum it up, I took a wonderful woman out tonight and had a great time getting to know her. She's special in so many ways. Who knows how serious we'll get, I'm just enjoying things as they come. But my time with her made me realize how much of a wound I still have from you and the importance of forgiving you so that she doesn't have to pay for you the whole time we're dating. Some day maybe we can heal our relationship fully, your response to this delegates that to some degree, but I more so know that hating you and constantly being angry at you is too much effort. Effort I can put into blessing Martha with a man who cares for and honors her the way he's supposed to. -Lugnut

Despite all these deaths, he remained alive, his body healing and rejuvenating itself every time. As he sat there, lost in thought, a young woman approached him cautiously. "Excuse me," she said, "are you alright?" The immortal looked up and smiled at her. "Yes, I'm fine," he said. "Just lost in thought." The woman sat down beside him and asked, "What are you thinking about?" The immortal hesitated for a moment before replying, "Death. Specifically, my own deaths." The woman looked surprised. "You've died? How is that possible?" The immortal let out a small chuckle. "I am blessed or cursed with immortality, depending on how you look at it. I have died countless times, but I always emerge from each death with a renewed vigor." The woman looked at him in awe. "That must be incredible. To experience death and yet live on." The immortal shook his head. "It's not as glamorous as it seems. Each time I die, I lose a part of myself. A memory, a feeling, a sense of who I am. It's like being born again and again, but with less each time." The woman looked at him with empathy. "I'm sorry," she said. "That must be hard." The immortal smiled wistfully. "It is. But I have learned to appreciate the time I have, to cherish each moment as if it were my last. Because one day, it will be."

article: "So essentially," Mr. Kramer concluded. "Nature tends toward chaos. In other words, things don't build themselves up they break down over time." Ray had not been paying attention up to that point. Nothing unusual there. The young eighth grader's apathy toward school was clearly reflected by the numerous doodles on the work he turned in. "What is the formula that relates force to mass and acceleration?" Why, two stick figures sword fighting while the crude contour of a scantily-clad prize-woman spectates next to question two, of course. "Ray!" Mr. Kramer sternly gripped the boy's attention." "Shit. " Ray thought to himself. "In your own words, could you repeat what I just told the class?" "Um so, basically, like nature builds up, and uh, then chaos, like you know, the chaotic nature, uh like, breaks. Over time." The boy's wandering mind fumbled around trying to piece together what he had heard in his peripheral like an incompetent secretary hulling heaps of cluttered papers. Old Peaches and Krame sighed through his thick, scraggly mustache. Certainly not the first time Ray had dragged out such a reaction from his teachers. "That is the exact opposite of what I said. At least I think it is. Nature does not magically build itself up, it breaks down. Order becomes disorder, and it takes a lot of work to make it work the other way around. You see Jenga blocks fall down on their own, not assemble themselves into a structured tower, right?" "Stranger things have happened." murmured a voice from the back that barely broke through. The small, brisk voice came from under the sweatshirt hood of the quiet girl who had always sat in the back. No one knew her name except Kramer, and even he could barely remember. Being the first time anyone had really heard the girl talk, an awkward tension overtook the room for a few cold moments. Luckily, the bell rang not long after. Ray, of course, wasted no time in making his escape while the teacher was distracted by whats-her-face. The boy nearly skipped his way out of the room with crumpled papers in hand, some falling to the ground and trailing behind him. Along with the rest of the troupe, the quiet young girl trotted out the door. On her way out, she picked up a few of Ray's papers, admiring his ever so masterful depictions of Darth Vader playing drums and a dragon burning down question seven. She couldn't help but grin at the juvenile scrawlings. Peering up at Ray, now distant at the other end of the hall, she was suddenly overtaken by a strange inspiration. Something about that strange young man that practically bled with apathy called out to her. It was the first time in her life that such a feeling had struck her, but it was strong. It was a siren's song that she couldn't ignore, and so she set her mind to do something she hadn't done in years make a new friend. The ancient swing creaked above Ray as he gently thrust his legs back and forth in a mindless, autonomous motion. After school, he would always venture to the local playground near his house to sit on the swing set and play his Game Boy while his stacks of undone homework practically pushed a hole through the hypothetical ceiling. The bottom of his shoes brushed against he chips of wood or whatever they were below him. He was too distracted by his game to give it much thought, but his subconscious couldn't help but remember a time when his tiny, kindergarten feet didn't even reach the ground on that very swing. Ray was a creature of habit. For as long as he could remember, he had been going to the same park, sitting on the same swing, pattering away at the buttons of the same Game Boy. He remembered a time when he wasn't the biggest kid at the park, when other kids his age would actually sit next to him on the swing set. He supposed the first graders were a little off-put by the presence of a "big kid" on their turf. They didn't understand why he didn't put down his Game Boy like the rest of his friends and go chase girls and yucky stuff like that. In the back of his mind, Ray wondered about that too. He sometimes wondered what would happen if he put down the Game Boy and went out and struck a conversation with one of his peers. But, ever a man of integrity, Ray always reverted back to his life's philosophy: meh. The sounds of the screeching swing mingled with the static-laden beeps and boops of his classic Game Boy. Sweet sounds of nostalgia to Ray, sounds he practically bathed in everyday after school sounds soon polluted by the distant chatter of a few familiar voices. They were distant, but Ray knew they were coming. He hadn't looked around to notice that the park was empty today, which meant one thing Trevor. Whenever the local park was empty usually every Monday the friendly neighborhood eight grade psychopath Trevor would come to finalize the various transactions he had made throughout the week with his humble weed selling enterprise. He was quite the young entrepreneur in spite of his rotting teeth and animalistic bursts of rage. Having at least (or most) half a brain, Ray opted to get the hell out of dodge before Trevor and his crew of eighties movie bullies showed up to cause some trouble. He only had so much time, though. The heralding sounds of "no way, dude!" and "fuckin' sick, bro!" were fast approaching. Ray started toward his house, walking as fast as he could without looking like a coward running for his milk money, which was essentially what he was doing. Just as he thought he was in the safety zone where Trevor couldn't smell him out, Ray heard the gut-wrenching utterance of "hey! Ain't he that fuckin' faggot kid who plays a Game Boy at the park?" Ray cocked his head behind him to see how close the Cobra Kai had gotten. Still walking, though, the side of his head collided right with the bar of the jungle gym, followed by a thick thud against the ground. It didn't take long before Trevor and his posse were looming over the young boy's body. He was fine, but it was too late to spring back up to his feet now. "Well, well, well, what do we have here?" Trevor said in the most cliche way imaginable. Ray fought back the cringe he felt from Trevor's Hollywood bully douchebaggery and kept his mouth clamped the best he could. "What's this?" Asked Trevor rhetorically, even though he would never learn would rhetorically means. "Looks like an old Game Boy to me. I used to have one of these. When I was five!" Trevor and his entourage burst into hysterics. "Hey! Don't touch my shit, man! Come on!" "Oh, you mean this?" Trevor yielded the Game Boy to gravity as he met it midair with the tip of his old, crusty boot. The Game Boy soared toward the jungle gym, ricocheting off one of the corner bars and shattering into fragments. Ray's face melted into despair. "What the hell, dude! I didn't even save!" Trevor and his buddies fell back into a fit of laughter. Not wanting to divert anymore time away from their business, the bullies walked back over to the other side of the playground to meet with their first client. They had to tarnish their professionalism by being late, after all. Ray stared at the shrapnel hopelessly mingled with the playground's dirt and wood chips. He was flooded with the horror of losing all those years of memories in one second of senseless violence. Sitting up on the ground, his muscles gave way to the weight of defeat and let his back plummet to the wood chips. As he stared hopelessly into the sky, a shadow engulfed the sun above him, approaching as silently as it now stood looming. Ray's eyes flickered, trying to make out the details of the figure hidden in the shade of the figure. He barely assembled the puzzle enough to recognize her as the girl from his science class. He quickly stood up, soon feeling an eerie sensation wash over him. "Oh, uh, hey. You're, uh..." Ray scrambled in his brain to find her name in his memory. "You dropped some of your papers." Said the girl, extending her sleeve-draped hand holding the worksheets that bore his timeless masterpieces. "Oh. Um, thanks." The girl diverted her gaze to the shattered Game Boy. "I'm sorry about your game." Ray sighed. "It's alright, I guess. Nothing I can do about it now. Just sucks that I probably have to play catch or some shit as an excuse not to do my homework now." Silent, the girl walked over to the remnants of Ray's handheld. She stooped down slowly, in a creepy, mechanical way. Ray steadily creeped around to the side at a distance to see what she was about to do. Steadily, the girl inhaled, more so than usual, like she was about to blow out birthday candles. A few strange, suspenseful moments after she had reached the apex, she released her deep breath onto the ground where the Game Boy had crashed. At first, nothing happened. Ray didn't think he could be even more off-put by this girl, but she managed to raise the bar. Just as Ray was about to back away and head for the hills, not wanting any weird voodoo shit on his head, he saw the bits of plastic and circuitry crawl toward one another. Bit by bit, Ray watched every little trinket and component reassemble itself into its original spot. The circuits realigned, the batteries reverted into their proper spots, and even the crack in the screen sealed back up as if it was never there. Finally, Ray saw the beaming scarlet eye of the power light flicker back on, and the exact pixels that he had seen right before the system's destruction repopulated the screen. Ray's jaw had practically fallen off its hinges. The girl stood up and offered the Game Boy back to its rightful owner. "H-how did you...... It's back to normal! You fixed it like magic!" "Normal? I wouldn't say that. I did more than just fix it." To be continued.....

As the days passed, I started to regain some of my strength. Nurses and doctors would come by to check on me and give me updates. They told me that I had been in a coma for a few weeks and that I had a long road to recovery, but I would get there eventually. Although I was grateful to be alive, I couldn't shake off the feeling that something was off. I felt like I was forgetting something important, but I couldn't put my finger on it. article: In certain applications, relay terminals can be employed to simultaneously deliver information and energy to a designated receiver and a radio frequency (RF) energy harvester, respectively. In such scenarios, the relay terminal acts as a mediator between the transmitter and the receiver. It receives the signal from the transmitter and uses its own energy to amplify and re-transmit the signal to the receiver. At the same time, the RF energy harvester captures energy from the transmitted signal and uses it to power the relay terminal and other low-power electronic devices. This type of system is commonly used in wireless sensor networks, where sensors located in remote and inaccessible areas require a reliable and long-lasting source of power. By harnessing RF energy, these systems can operate without the need for battery replacements or other external power sources, making them an economical and sustainable solution. Overall, relay terminals play a crucial role in enabling the transmission and harvesting of energy in wireless communication systems, paving the way for new and innovative applications in a variety of industries.

article: The weight of the gun in Carrie's hand was more than she could bear. The kitchen was a mess. Blood was splattered across the floor in criss cross patterns and dark red hand prints stained cabinets and doors around her. Not far from where Carrie paced the corpse of a dog was already starting to bloat, and she tried not to look at it. It was difficult. The smell was unbearable. "What are you doing here?" A voice suddenly asked from the back door. Carrie spun around on her heel, her weapon pointed at the intruder. It was only Jaime. She lowered the weapon and huffed, "I'm waiting." "You don't have to. Look. You can get out of here, Carrie. You can leave - we both know "Mark is upstairs. I told him I'd wait and I'm waiting." Carrie sneered. Jaime took a step towards her and reached out for her hand, "But you don't have to!" Carrie jerked back but Jaime snatched her wrist in his palm and squeezed, "Stop it! Listen, we both know what's going to happen here. There is nothing either of us can do to stop it. Now you can leave if you want to. I'm telling you that." "I'm supposed to stay. It's supposed to happen. You're supposed to "Shut up." Jaime hissed, "I'm not going to." "You will." Carrie grumbled, "We're not writing this, someone else is. We're not in control." A loud snarl erupted from the basement beneath, and Carrie jumped. Jaime kept his hold on her, "I can push you down those stairs too." "You wouldn't dare." "We both know how this is going to end." A loud crash suddenly sounded from upstairs. Feet shuffled, and Mark's low voice cried out for help upstairs. Carrie moved towards the stairs to meet him, but Jaime jerked her arm back and kept her at his side. Carrie yelled in frustration and tried to pull away, jerking her arm back until her shoulder ached, "LET ME GO!" "No!" Jaime snapped, "That wasn't supposed to happen." Carrie froze and looked up. The shuffling stopped, and the house went dead quiet. Jaime let go of Carrie's wrist, "What are you going to do?" "I'm going to keep going. We have to move forward. We have to make sure everything goes just like it's supposed to and "Everything is fucked," Jaime spat, "You're just a means to an end! You think anyone cares about you? article: The war had been going on for generations. Entire lifecycles lost to this futile waste of resources. At this point in time we should have known better. The moment we were able to explaine our propostion to them they accepted. That should have been the second red flag. Their preparations started immediately after we gave them access to our method of faster than light travel. The humans send a group of millitary experts and weapons sepcialists to talk to our scientist and strategists. They even offered to take up refugees, some of us even chose to relocate to their planet, believing it was safer to hide close to our enemy. With our help and knowledge they immediately started to assemble warships armed to their teeth. Specifically our knowledge of superconductors and magnetism enabled them to build weapons we had never even dreamt of. They refitted some of our old ships and even started to build their own. Mounting giant weapons on some of them others were designed to host hundreds of smaller spacecraft just large enough for one human. After our negotioations they told us about their history, and apparently they had been at war with each other for most of their history. Sometimes over resources othertimes over mating rights the reasons were endless, the time this species had spend thinking about diffrent ways of killing each other was unparalleled. And so they came up with the most horiffic weapons. However building a fleet takes time and so the war between us and the Kar'Sai waged on. And it was going terrible for us. We had lost contact to almost all of our colonies and had sensor data on a very large Kar'Sai fleet that was making their way to our home system. They entered our system and all of us abandoned the hope that the humans would arrive in time to save us. Our last defensive effort failed and we were ready to surrender the moment the Kar'Sai ships aligned to bombard our home planet. That was the moment the humans arrived. They had prepared an ambush and the Kar'Sai were not prepared for a real confrontation. And even for a people as warlike as the Kar'Sai the humans were no match. They had armed their ships to the teeth with large preojectile weapons and very precise Laser weaponry. They tore some of the Kar'Sai ships to pieces others were almost melted by the large amount of plasma bombs that were dropped on them by the tiny, one man spacecraft. The humans even took some of the Kar'Sai ships in melee reclaiming them. They had used our technology to build personalized armored suits for their boarding squads. That day th humans had not only saved our home system but they had also made it a witness to the worst slaughter the galaxy had ever seen. The humans intented to kill every last Kar'Sai. Later they told us that this number didn't even compare to the wars on their home planet. We were chilled, the largest fight in our history had killed about 10,000 individuals. And so the humans continued to liberate all of our colonies and anybody else subjugated by the Kar'Sai. We were delighted and terrified by their efffeciency. But suddenly everything changed, for the first time the Kar'Sai had managed to get in contact with the humans, and the fighting halted. They realized something. They were cloesely related. article: Deep video recognition is more computationally expensive than image recognition, especially on large-scale datasets like Kinetics. The gradients from each worker are then averaged and used to update the global model parameters. This method can be efficient for models with large numbers of parameters, but can be limited by the communication overhead between workers. Another approach is model parallelism, where different segments of the model are trained on different workers. This method can be more efficient for models with large numbers of layers, but can be limited by the memory constraints of each worker. Finally, hybrid approaches can be used, which combine both data and model parallelism to take advantage of the benefits of both approaches. Overall, distributed training methods are essential for training deep video recognition models on large-scale datasets, as they allow for improved scalability and reduced training time.

Repeat steps 4-6 for populations I3, 4,...,N, using the sample mean and variance from the previous sample to determine the appropriate sample size for the next population. Note that this method assumes that the populations are independent and identically distributed (iid), and that the samples are drawn with replacement. article: Evaluating conjunctive queries and solving constraint satisfaction problems are fundamental problems in database theory and artificial intelligence, respectively. These problems are NP-hard, so that several research efforts have been made to find efficient algorithms for solving them. Some commonly used techniques include: 1. Backtracking: This is a systematic search algorithm for solving constraint satisfaction problems. It involves starting with an initial assignment and recursively exploring different possible values for each variable until a solution is found. If no solution is found, the algorithm backtracks to the last decision point and tries a different value. 2. Branch and Bound: This is another search algorithm that works by dividing the search space into smaller subspaces and exploring them systematically. It is particularly effective for solving optimization problems, where the goal is to find the best solution among a set of possible solutions. 3. Constraint Propagation: This technique involves using logical inference rules to eliminate inconsistent values from the search space. For example, if a variable can only take on two possible values, and one of those values is already assigned to another variable, then the other value can be eliminated from consideration. 4. Heuristics: These are rule-of-thumb strategies that can be used to guide the search process. For example, the Minimum Remaining Values heuristic suggests starting with the variable that has the fewest possible values remaining to explore. Overall, solving NP-hard problems requires a combination of mathematical and computational techniques, and often involves a trade-off between finding an optimal solution and finding a solution quickly.

I had offered Barbara a ride when I passed her house, but she was too frantic. I hadn't seen her this frazzled since the Black Friday Target fiasco of 2005. I continued on my way down to my favorite bar. I checked in to see if Lou was alright. He was pretty crazed too. The TV was ranting about all of this insanity being the Apocalypse or something. I didn't really pay it too much mind. I tried to calm a very distraught, sobbing Lou. He refused to move from behind the bar. I sighed and decided it best to keep on driving. If this truly was the "End of Time," then I thought it would be nice to take a scenic route so I can pass by the beaches. It would've been such a shame to pass up the opportunity considering it was such a beautiful day. I called my family members while driving. All of them were hysterical. I reassured them that even if this was the end, we all loved each other and that's all that really matters. Plus, we got to go on a wonderful family cruise last summer that visited the European countries of Greece, Italy, and Turkey. I very much believe that it healed our family in a lot of ways. Knowing that we have those precious memories makes up for not being together right now. Oh my, I better finish writing this little entry. You see, I've been an optimist about this whole ordeal. I've really believed that this would all pass. However, there is a quite terrifying tsunami headed my way as I type this. Not to mention, I passed many a house on fire and a few out of place tornadoes. My drive yesterday eventually led me here, a secluded beach somewhere in Northern California. I found a little shack and decided to write a little bit before kicking the bucket. Now although my optimism may be frowned upon by some possibly many, I must let you the reader understand that I was never completely shielded from reality. I knew there was a good chance that this really was the end. I only kept my hope alive because it would ensure, perhaps, a happier and more tranquil death. I am no fool. Death is an inevitable part of life. I am just content that I got to drive down this gorgeous Californian coast on a beautiful Spring day, got to call my family and tell them I love them, and got to find this quaint beach the last place I will ever visit. Here I have spent my last moments documenting my experience in the last 24 hours with a view like no other and my dog by my side. The wave is quite high now. Wow. Look at it! Must be a thousand stories high! Slightly sad now that I couldn't be on the coast of Hawaii or some other island. The water would have probably been a lot bluer and clearer! Oh well. You win some and you lose some. Ah! So my optimism remains! Even with this impressive wave about to consume me and Scoobs. A wise man by the name of Plato once said, "We can easily forgive a child who is afraid of the dark; the real tragedy of life is when men are afraid of the light." I can't say for sure Plato is talking about the afterlife. I was never the smartest cookie in the cookie jar. However for the purpose of my tale, I believe that is indeed what he is talking about. My optimism has allowed me to reject this idea of fear. I am excited for the light. I welcome it. Sometimes when I worked images flashed across my mind, visions of places that looked nothing like my cell or the worksite, visions of people without uniforms or shaved heads. The words were foreign to me, yet they lingered in my head with strange persistence. A male lion weighs three hundred to five hundred pounds. Nitroglycerine explodes in response to heat. Rick Dall sells STF armour. I started carving a notch into my cell wall every time I was awoken by the bell. But sometimes we awoke to the sun's light, other times there was still darkness. The passage of time, and the length of our days, was skewed. On the day when I scratched the twenty-fifth line on my wall, someone new was brought to the camp. He was tall, taller than even I was. article: To support a freight carrier in a combinatorial transport auction, we proposes an exact and two heuristic strategies for bidding on subsets of requests. The exact bidding strategy is based on an integer linear programming model that aims to maximize the carrier's profit while satisfying a set of constraints, including capacity and time constraints. The model determines the optimal combination of requests to bid on that will provide the highest profit. The first heuristic strategy is a greedy algorithm that selects requests in descending order of their marginal profit, which is the difference between the profit of the current set of requests and the profit of the same set without the last request. This strategy is simple and fast but may not always find the optimal solution. The second heuristic strategy is a genetic algorithm that starts with a population of random solutions and iteratively evolves them through selection, crossover, and mutation operations. This strategy can explore multiple solutions and may find better solutions than the greedy algorithm, but it is more computationally expensive. By using a combination of these strategies, the freight carrier can bid on subsets of requests efficiently and effectively, leading to increased profits and better utilization of resources.

Of course, he spent half the classes sitting outside, or outside the headmaster's office. That was the thing with teachers: you never won, even when you were right. Nothing to be gained, but the glory. Because, really, everyone knew James. He was a legend that would get passed on until the day Mrs. Gresnich kicked the bucket. That we stood there at the memorial, and people would come over to see him, well, that spoke to the truth of it. He didn't look particularly happy about it, but he shared a smile and a handshake with them. In a way, his arrival surprised me. I was stuck in the neighbourhood, taking over my old man's shop. He was half the world away, more or less, working over in London. Surprised us all that, somehow he'd gotten into a half-decent uni and continued on from there. Never expected the old James to do that, when he could barely add two and two to make five - he normally got seven. So, I'd nearly missed him when he turned up in a suit and tie, hair neatly combed and expression sombre. Clapped him on the shoulder, and he lit up when he saw me. Hugged me hard, not like back in the day. Made me realise how much time had passed, and how much it could do. Basically took a lump of a boy and chiselled him into a man. Not like me, sitting on my arse all day selling cuts of meat for a meagre living. He'd brought along one looker of a wife, too. Legs for days and all that, but she seemed sweet. The two of us fell in like old buddies, as she drank up the stories of our misspent youth. He didn't intervene at all, but looked decidedly uncomfortable with the memories, no doubt something he wanted to distance himself from. But, well, where we all stood, that was a reminder that our past wasn't there to be forgotten. In their own way, many people had shaped us into who we'd become. The time I'd spent with James taught me what it meant to be a hero. No one cared about men in tights saving the world, but a mate that would tell old Mrs. Gresnich to bugger off when she set her sights on some poor, snivelling lad? Yeah, I'd spent a lot of my misspent youth wanting to be like James. A recurring dream of mine had been to turn up at our old school, walk into that dusty maths room, and tell her what I bloody well thought of her. Of course, I'd never actually do it. James was a hero because he was a puny git with a voice that cracked every other sentence. A hulk of a man like me shouting at an old lady, well, I'd be lucky if I got off without the coppers being called. James probably didn't think of himself as a hero either, not at the time and not after all that time. I dunno if he was ever scared, probably was. Always grinning, always scared, always standing up. A kind of trinity of hero-ness. I asked his missus what he was up to these days, and she rubbed her belly and spoke of moving out to a small town, far from the smoggy streets of the capital. Laughed, and threw in my thought that our old town had its charms, and she laughed too. James didn't, but he hadn't laughed at all, over the afternoon. The merriment died out during the service, and we wandered around the three of us, saying our kind words to the family. Of course, James couldn't catch a break there either. " James, as in James Williams? " He nodded, awkwardly avoiding meeting the daughter's eyes. " She spoke fondly of you, " she said, smiling what looked like a natural one, and not the fake, mourning one exchanged with the other guests. " She did? " he asked, surprised. Chuckling, she softly shrugged. " Well, she spoke of you. At least, she kept complaining about you and your legacy. " " I see, " he said, bowing his head. " I'm sorry, I was a troublesome child for her. " " No, no, " she said. " It got her fired up. Even in her last days, she'd perk right up when it came to telling us all what an ungrateful child you were. So, I'm thankful for your trouble, we all are. " Say what you will about Mrs. Gresnich, but her daughter was wonderful. I hadn't thought James felt guilty about those years, but she'd cut that all away. I could see the difference in him, and the smile he had was like when he spotted me. " I'm thankful for her trouble too, " he said softly. She laughed back, and replied, " She'd be glad to hear that. " And, we all left it at that. Me, him and his missus took off to a nearby pub. I dunno if I was spoiling plans or anything, but he needed a friend. Not to talk to or anything, just to keep her from badgering him. So, I did my best to keep her attention, telling her many tales about that old dragon of a maths teacher we'd had, while tears swelled in his eyes, and did my best to cough over any sniffles he did. It took a good half hour before he started regaining his composure, and a moment's reprieve was granted when she excused herself. James, he'd really grown up since those days. Or, maybe he hadn't, and I'd just been too busy admiring him.'Cause, he'd always been a kind person, good-hearted I should say. So, having such a nice and caring wife, well, that wasn't a surprise. And, getting emotional over how he treated Mrs. Gresnich, even if she'd deserved it, that wasn't a surprise once I'd thought about it. He reached over, and patted the top of my hand, before leaning back in his seat and staring at the ceiling. " Thanks, " he said. I smiled, taking a sip of something far less alcoholic than normal. But, my company was a pregnant lass and her designated driver, so I could put aside my usual for the day. " No problem. " His head tilted to the side, towards the bathrooms, and then back to how it was. " You know, Mrs. Gresnich was the bitchiest bitch who ever bitched. " I laughed. " Yeah, she was. " " But, " he said, and his voice grew strained from just that word. " Whenever I asked her for help, she didn't tell me to bugger off, or ask me what the point of helping an idiot was, or say it was too late for me to start now. " Ah, yeah, most of our teachers were like that. Oh sure, if you were a sweet, young girl, they'd help you out. Boys were a waste of time, couldn't be bothered to listen the first time, teachers had better things to do with their time. Really, it was a surprise any of us lads had even made it to uni, though I guess some of them actually did pay attention in class, and did their homework, and studied at home. " She never complained, just helped me. When no one thought I was worth a minute of their time, she helped me get into university. " I doubt anyone had ever been brave enough to ask her for help before. Not even heroes asked dragons for help. Heroes were there to slay dragons, to fight against them to the death and claim the treasure. Maybe get the girl, who had been trapped in a tower for some unknown reason. " Really, it's thanks to her I'm happy today, " he said, softly. " Thanks to her, I met my wife, found my dream job. " " Yeah, you really pulled your act together, " I said. " Hardly recognise you. " He laughed, nodding his head. " I always wanted to come back, and say thank you to her. But, I kept thinking she wasn't going anywhere. For some reason, I never thought she'd die. " " Same here. " Looking off the side, his missus emerged, walking over with the barest signs of a bulging tummy. Only a few months in, so another half a year or so to go. And, that led to me thinking about what Mrs. Gresnich had been like as a kid. For some reason, I thought she must have been like James. A wild child, full of vigour and more questions than answers. The tomboy who shouted down the boys that bullied girls, and gave them a good kicking if they answered back. I dunno why I thought that, but it was something about how he was the only one who could confront her. Kindred spirits, from different times. So, if she was a dragon, then surely he was too. Watching him dote on his missus, while he'd been so lost minutes prior, warmed my grimy heart. A real good guy, and I guess Mrs. Gresnich had known, even if she'd been a real nasty woman, who picked on kids until they cried. She was definitely a dragon, through and through. Him? He had the soul of a dragon, but the will of a hero.

article: It is prohibitively expensive to annotate a large-scale video-based person re-identification (re-ID) dataset, which makes fully supervised methods inapplicable to real-world deployment. How to maximally reduce the annotation cost while retaining the re-ID performance becomes an interesting problem. In this paper, we address this problem by integrating an active learning scheme into a deep learning framework. Noticing that the truly matched tracklet-pairs, also denoted as true positives (TP), are the most informative samples for our re-ID model, we propose a sampling criterion to choose the most TP-likely tracklet-pairs for annotation. A view-aware sampling strategy considering view-specific biases is designed to facilitate candidate selection, followed by an adaptive resampling step to leave out the selected candidates that are unnecessary to annotate. Our method learns the re-ID model and updates the annotation set iteratively. The re-ID model is supervised by the tracklets' pesudo labels that are initialized by treating each tracklet as a distinct class. With the gained annotations of the actively selected candidates, the tracklets' pesudo labels are updated by label merging and further used to re-train our re-ID model. While being simple, the proposed method demonstrates its effectiveness on three video-based person re-ID datasets. Experimental results show that less than 3 pairwise annotations are needed for our method to reach comparable performance with the fully-supervised setting.

A few of the students could not resist moving their eyes away from the white board to look at him. The teacher jumped up and furrowed his brow, his mouth frowning and baring his sharpened teeth. "What was that?" "N-nothing, sir, I The resounding crack reverberated throughout the room, sending the vibrations through every rib of every student in the room. His hand had flown out in a flash, and in the briefest moment, the boy was on the ground. His hand didn't move to rub his cheek, and he only got up again, staring straight ahead. He straightened out his shirt, his pants, and moved his head up to face forwards, not speaking. The teacher grinned, his eyes almost glinting in the flourescent light, and raised his hand once more when suddenly the whiteboard behind him exploded. For the third time that hour, the sound echoed around the room. This time it was stronger than any sniff or slap, and desks were thrown off the ground and onto the back room. The students could not hold it any more, and two of them let out a groan, the rest trembling and biting their lips. Out from the debris of the whiteboard stepped a man, dressed in complete glowing white and wearing a cape that flapped and fluttered despite no wind. "Halt! In the name of academic justice!" The teacher turned around, cringing at the light the man casted on him. The light made the shadows around the teacher's sunken eyes darker, and his already pale skin paler, transforming his face into an almost skeletal mockery of its original. "And who are you?" There was a sharp whisper of metal edge against leather as the man drew a meter stick from behind him, sheathed in his belt. The teacher took a few steps back, his words failing him as his lips quivered. The student standing in front looked at the shaking teacher, and he dared to move his eyebrows up in surprise. The teacher didn't hit him this time. The caped man stepped towards the teacher, brandishing his ruler. "You have committed an immeasurable sin." He held the ruler in front of the teacher, whose pants were now wet with his fear. "Get away! I'll call the police!" The teacher moved his hand towards the phone on his desk, but the man continued onwards. "And it has come time for me to rule you and with a quick motion of his sharpened meter stick he slashed downwards, cutting off the hand that the teacher had stretched out, incompetent of teaching!" The teacher screeched and clutched the bloody stump that was his hand. Tears flooded down his bony cheeks, and he kneeled down, screaming. "What have you done?" "I am the White Board Man, and it's time to be taught a lesson." He grinned, his pearly teeth shining in the unnatural luminescence of his costume, and raised his meter stick high. "It looks like someone has to school you in manners, young man!" "No! Please! I learned!" He clutched his bloodied wrist tightly, but it wasn't enough to stop the spurting that now dirtied the floor underneath them. "Please!" The caped man shook his head. "You haven't learned. I'm sorry, but I have to pass judgement. With my meter stick of justice, I declare you..." His stick swung down towards the sobbing teacher, cleaving straight into his neck and passing clear through it. " ..... failed." The teacher's head dropped off his shoulders, flopping onto the floor in the bloody mess. The superhero turned around, sheathing his measurement stick and placing his arms on his hips to survey the students. The desks were put back, except for two students who were pinned to the back wall by their desks. The students did not move, and no other student had helped them. Everything was neatly arranged, and even the student who had been failed was at his desk. One of the students, a little girl with two pig tails and big glasses, raised her hand. The superhero coughed, looking around at the kids, who all stared forwards, arms on the desk in the exact same way. He shifted, expecting a response. After a few brief moments, he pointed towards the girl. "Yes, child? I have saved you all from the tyranny of this teacher, what say you?" "Are you the substitute teacher, sir?" There was a moment's pause. And then he laughed, a hearty laugh that echoed once more through the room. "No! My job here is done, I have ended unfair treatment, and now I must go to right more wrongs in many many more classroms just like this one." The girl nodded, and placed her arms down gently, exactly in the same position as all the other students. The superhero took one last look around the room, smiling, and jumped back into the whiteboard with a whish of his cape. article: Great successes of deep neural networks have been witnessed in various real applications. Many algorithmic and implementation techniques have been developed; however, theoretical understanding of many aspects of deep neural networks is still limited. One of the challenges in deep learning is determining the optimal architecture of the neural network, including the number of layers, the number of nodes in each layer, and the type of activation function to be used. Another challenge is the difficulty in interpreting how the network arrives at its output, which is known as the black box problem. This makes it challenging to understand why certain decisions are made by the network, especially in cases where the network makes incorrect predictions. Additionally, deep neural networks can require substantial computational resources and large datasets to train effectively, which can be expensive and time-consuming. Despite these challenges, deep neural networks continue to be a promising tool for a wide range of applications, including image recognition, natural language processing, and speech recognition. Ongoing research seeks to address these challenges and improve the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of deep neural networks.

article: Rain pattered down on the streets and sidewalks of Philadelphia as I walked from my apartment to work. It was routine, and some faces I recognized amid the strangers going about their own business. In the doorway to his bakery stood Mr. Candela, the old Italian baker who'd let me rent from him for a few months. I shot him a wave, and he grinned that toothy grin he had. Halfway to work the rain began to slow, degenerating into a mist. Off toward Jersey I heard thunder rumbling and grinned. Jersey is where bad weather belongs. They're made for each other. I always saw her around here. A girl with light grey hair, her eyes a shade lighter. It never struck me to talk to her. She was a goddess, I was a mortal. A little overweight, scruffy beard covering a budding under-chin, glasses. My prime days physically speaking were almost a decade ago as a running back on my high school football team. Adulthood hit me hard. Stress, man. College, debt, hunting for a job, retiring nightly to an empty apartment (or bringing some short-term girl back from time to time) all took their toll on me. Periodically I'd get depressed by it all, generally within a few days of paying what I could off the top of my student loans. Today, though, as I approached the park, I wanted to see her again. In the least sexual sense and in the most sexual sense I found her form pleasing to the eye. She was beautiful, but something told me that I would love her for more than that..... if I could ever open my mouth and say something. I began to lose hope when at last she rounded the corner and walked toward me. Her cell phone was rooted to her ear, hidden beneath those grey locks, curled at the ends today. She wore a long raincoat over black jeans and a white shirt. As always, my heart fluttered at the sight of her but my brain stalled out. I just glanced up at her, and back down before she saw me looking. We crossed paths at the entrance to an alley. Fortunately I'd looked away, like a damn coward, because I saw the car backing down the alley and reached for her to move her aside- the phone was distracting her, and I didn't think the driver could see us because his brake lights were still dim. My hand brushed her raincoat and immediately my eyes whited out. Still, my momentum carried us backward and the car passed us by (I assume) without any harm. By then, my eyes adjusted. Something happened. I looked at the girl, who was blinking and looking around wide-eyed like I was. The world had changed! Black had become something else, and the shades of grey everywhere had turned into other colors, I guessed, but to describe them would be impossible. The world was bright! Our eyes met, hers the same color as the sky above us. There were no words, not at first. It struck me then what had happened. Years ago my parents had told me about this, and I'm sure every parent had said something to the same effect: "Once you find the right girl, she'll bring color to your world." I had no idea it was literal.

article: We introduce novel dynamic oracles for training two of the most accurate known shift-reduce algorithms for constituent parsing: the top-down and in-order transition-based parsers. article: Context: In C, low-level errors, such as buffer overflow and use-after-free, are a major problem, as they cause security vulnerabilities and hard-to-find bugs. C lacks automatic checks, and programmers cannot apply defensive programming techniques because objects (e.g., arrays or structs) lack run-time information about bounds, lifetime, and types. Inquiry: Current approaches to tackling low-level errors include dynamic tools, such as bounds or type checkers, that check for certain actions during program execution. If they detect an error, they typically abort execution. Although they track run-time information as part of their runtimes, they do not expose this information to programmers. Approach: We devised an introspection interface that allows C programmers to access run-time information and to query object bounds, object lifetimes, object types, and information about variadic arguments. This enables library writers to check for invalid input or program states and thus, for example, to implement custom error handling that maintains system availability and does not terminate on benign errors. As we assume that introspection is used together with a dynamic tool that implements automatic checks, errors that are not handled in the application logic continue to cause the dynamic tool to abort execution. Knowledge: Using the introspection interface, we implemented a more robust, source-compatible version of the C standard library that validates parameters to its functions. The library functions react to otherwise undefined behavior; for example, they can detect lurking flaws, handle unterminated strings, check format string arguments, and set errno when they detect benign usage errors. Grounding: Existing dynamic tools maintain run-time information that can be used to implement the introspection interface, and we demonstrate its implementation in Safe Sulong, an interpreter and dynamic bug-finding tool for C that runs on a Java Virtual Machine and can thus easily expose relevant run-time information. Importance: Using introspection in user code is a novel approach to tackling the long-standing problem of low-level errors in C. As new approaches are lowering the performance overhead of run-time information maintenance, the usage of dynamic runtimes for C could become more common, which could ultimately facilitate a more widespread implementation of such an introspection interface.

Within five minutes a black car with tinted windows rolled up. Zach motioned for Barry to get in the car. The second Barry's ass hit the seat he was zapped by a taser and left senseless. He awoke in a small room with an open door. He walked out the door to a massive hive of humanity working on computers with giant screens overhead that had images of dragons, krakens, and other legendary beasts. Zach told him as he handed him a coffee. "What's with the weird pixie thing in the middle?" Barry said and suddenly klaxons began blaring and people started screaming and running in all directions. "You wish to be the champion? To save the world?" The little statue asked. "Don't talk to it!" Zach screamed, all sorts of devices began pointing at the statue, guns were being loaded and cocked all around the room. "Sure I'll save the world." Barry said. A bright light washed over him as he heard the screams from everyone in the building falling away. Suddenly Barry was alone in a giant arena. Then the dragon landed and the statue followed it. "Kill the dragon! Save the world! If dragon kill you everybody die!" The statue said gleefully. "I can't. I have no means to kill it. I'll just die the moment it attacks me. This isn't fair." "Fair?" the statue asked. "Yes fair. For something to be fair both sides have to have a chance to win." Barry said. In a blink suddenly the dragon was the size of a small house cat and Barry had a sword slung over his back and an AR-15 in his hands with three clips hanging from his belt. "Fair?!" The statue asked. "No, this isn't fair. I'll kill the dragon without any effort." "But this way you win! Everyone live!" The statue said. "Yes but that doesn't make it fair. Just because I'm now the one that's going to win doesn't mean it's right." Barry didn't know why he felt that explaining the concept of fairness to this alien being was more important then all life on the planet, but he had a feeling deep in his soul that coming to an understanding with this being was something that had to be done. Another flash of light. Now the dragon was roughly the size of a tiger, and one of the ammo clips Barry had was gone. "Fair?!" The statue asked. "Yeah, fair." Barry said with a nod. "Save the world!" the statue cheered. It then winked out of existence. The dragon jerked it's head back and blasted a wave of fire at Barry who jumped and rolled to the side. "Well I've got myself in it now." Barry said as he loaded his gun and opened fire. The duel to save the world had begun.

article: This paper introduces a video dataset of spatio-temporally localized Atomic Visual Actions (AVA). The AVA dataset densely annotates 80 atomic visual actions in 430 15-minute video clips, where actions are localized in space and time, resulting in 1.58M action labels with multiple labels per person occurring frequently. The key characteristics of our dataset are: (1) the definition of atomic visual actions, rather than composite actions; (2) precise spatio-temporal annotations with possibly multiple annotations for each person; (3) exhaustive annotation of these atomic actions over 15-minute video clips; (4) people temporally linked across consecutive segments; and (5) using movies to gather a varied set of action representations. This departs from existing datasets for spatio-temporal action recognition, which typically provide sparse annotations for composite actions in short video clips. AVA, with its realistic scene and action complexity, exposes the intrinsic difficulty of action recognition. To benchmark this, we present a novel approach for action localization that builds upon the current state-of-the-art methods, and demonstrates better performance on JHMDB and UCF101-24 categories. While setting a new state of the art on existing datasets, the overall results on AVA are low at 15.6 mAP, underscoring the need for developing new approaches for video understanding.

article: The rules of the St Petersburg lottery game, from Wikipedia: Consider the following game of chance: you pay a fixed fee to enter and then a fair coin is tossed . If the coin comes up tails, you receive a payout of 2 dollars and the game is over. If the coin comes up heads, you receive a payout of 2 dollars and the coin is tossed again. If the second toss is tails, you receive an additional payout of 4 dollars (for a total of 6 dollars) and the game is over. If the second toss is heads, you receive an additional payout of 2 dollars and the coin is tossed again. If the third toss is tails, you receive an additional payout of 8 dollars (for a total of 10 dollars) and the game is over. If the third toss is heads, you receive an additional payout of 2 dollars and the coin is tossed again, and so on. The game continues until the coin first comes up tails, at which point the game ends and you receive your payout.
